title: The Independent Band and LeBlanc's dance bookings across the lake
summary: Lineup of the Independent Band with Bunk, the Frits and Lorons, and LeBlanc's nightly dance circuit around Mandeville.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: They had the Independent Band. That's the band that Bunk played with them.
Oh Bunk played with that band.
Yeah that band. That's the band. They had a fine band. They had Isidore Fritz, Louis Fritz, his brother playing trombone, his daddy playing bass, old man Joe Fritz.
He had a bunk playing trumpet and this boy Leon Loron was playing guitar with him.

Leon Loron. He's still old guitar player there with him. And then Ralph used to play violin with my dad. His brother Ralph Loron used to play violin with my daddy. He was a great violinist too. Baye, you know. He played both the same thing. And the drummer, the drummer I tell you was playing with him was clay bad. Little clay bad. His name is Keglin Eddie's brother. He's dead now. He's late clay bad. Well that was they lined up. And they had a fine band. Normally they play all those old moments such as the Tiger, Rag.
Did they work over there very often?

Oh yeah they worked on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. When Buddy Petit came over to work, he usually worked about a week. He played the vicinity like he'd take us out there. After Buddy Petit, he worked for this fellow LeBlanc. Mr. LeBlanc, he's up there on, incidentally I saw him a few weeks ago, he's up there on Maple Street. So LeBlanc took them over there and had a station wagon, see. Now he booked dances every night, you know. He'd play one, on Monday night he'd play in Mandeville. On Saturday night, Tuesday night, no he'd play in Carpentry. On Wednesday night he'd go to Bougalusa, you understand? Well Thursday night he'd play in Picayune or something like that, see. And then he'd come back to Mandeville and they'd play Friday, Saturday and Sunday at Votran's place on the beach, you know on the lake there? Mandeville on the beach. But those other nights, he kept them busy, you know, because I used to go around with them and be the doorman for them, you know. They had a real good band, they had a really good jazz band.
